policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 23:2 reads "perverting our nation"; the possessive "our" renders ἡμῶν, which the omitting reading lacks.
Pure word order: φόρους Καίσαρι and Καίσαρι φόρους both yield ASV "to give tribute to Caesar"; English order is fixed by its own grammar.
ASV 23:2 has "and saying that he himself is Christ a king", coordinating the third participle with "and" exactly as the first two are joined; the omitting reading leaves λέγοντα asyndetic.
αὑτὸν and ἑαυτὸν are orthographic variants of the same reflexive; both give ASV "he himself".
ἠρώτησεν and ἐπηρώτησεν are both rendered "asked"; the compound prefix has no separate English exponent here.

ASV "teaching throughout all Judaea, and beginning from Galilee" joins coordinate participles with "and", which the ASV supplies freely in a participial series; the English does not settle whether καί stood before ἀρξάμενος.
ASV 23:6 reads "when Pilate heard it" with no object "Galilee"; the added Γαλιλαίαν would give "heard of Galilee", which the ASV does not print.
ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων and θέλων ἐξ ἱκανοῦ differ in order and in the number of the idiom, both yielding ASV "of a long time desirous". The only note on 23:8 is a greek_gloss on "miracle".
ASV 23:8 reads "because he had heard concerning him" with no object; the added πολλὰ would give "heard many things concerning him".

ASV 23:11 prints "and mocked him, and arraying him"; since the second "and" answers to no καί in any reading, the first "and" shows only that the ASV coordinates participles in English, not that καί stood in the text.
ASV "arraying him in gorgeous apparel" supplies the object English requires of "arraying"; the pronoun does not show whether αὐτόν stood with περιβαλὼν.
ASV 23:12 names "Herod and Pilate" in that order, matching Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος against the transposed reading.
αὑτούς, αὐτούς and ἑαυτούς are orthographic variants; all three give ASV "between themselves".
οὐθὲν and οὐδὲν are spelling variants of the same word; both give ASV "found no fault".

ASV 23:15 reads "for he sent him back unto us", and its textual_variant note relegates "I sent you to him" to the margin as the reading of many ancient authorities — the note maps the alternative onto r01 and confirms the text follows ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς.
ASV 23:16 ends "and release him", with no verse 17 content in the text; the ASV prints the Ἀνάγκην δὲ εἶχεν sentence nowhere in the verse.
Ἀνέκραγον and Ἀνέκραξαν are alternative aorists of the same verb; both give ASV "they cried out". The verse note concerns the insertion of verse 17, not this unit.
The article before the proper name Barabbas has no English exponent; ASV "release unto us Barabbas" is the same either way.
βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ and βεβλημένος εἰς φυλακήν both come out as ASV "was cast into prison"; the aspect and the ἐν/εἰς alternation leave no separate mark in the English.
ASV 23:20 opens "And Pilate spake unto them again"; the ASV renders inferential οὖν with "therefore", so the bare "And" answers to δέ.
ASV 23:20 reads "spake unto them again": the explicit indirect object renders αὐτοῖς, absent from the shorter reading.
Σταύρου (present) and Σταύρωσον (aorist) imperatives both give ASV "Crucify, crucify"; English imperatives carry no aspect.
ASV 23:23 ends "And their voices prevailed" with no mention of chief priests; the added καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων would appear as "and of the chief priests".
καὶ Πιλᾶτος and ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος both yield ASV "And Pilate gave sentence"; connective and article leave no distinguishing mark.
The presence or absence of the article with φυλακή is not visible in ASV "had been cast into prison".

Accusative Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον and genitive Σίμωνός τινος with ἐπιλαβόμενοι are case alternatives of one construction; ASV "laid hold upon one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country" fits either.
ASV 23:27 reads "of women who bewailed and lamented him" without "also"; the added καί would give "who also bewailed".
The article with the proper name Ἰησοῦς has no English exponent; ASV "But Jesus turning unto them" is the same either way.
The article in the beatitude is not rendered distinctly; ASV "Blessed are the barren" fits the articular and anarthrous readings alike.
ἔθρεψαν (nourished) and ἐθήλασαν (suckled) are both covered by ASV "the breasts that never gave suck"; the English idiom does not choose between them.
ASV "in the green tree" supplies the English definite article the phrase requires; the presence or absence of τῷ with ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ is not thereby settled.
ASV "two others, malefactors" reorders and repunctuates to avoid classing Jesus with them — an English rendering choice; it does not track whether δύο stood before or after κακοῦργοι.
ἦλθον and ἀπῆλθον both come out as ASV "when they came unto the place"; the compound adds nothing the English marks. The verse note explains the Latin name Calvary.

ASV 23:34 prints "And Jesus said, Father, forgive them..." in the text and notes only that some ancient authorities omit it; both candidates contain the same words, differing in editorial bracketing, which no English rendering can distinguish.
ASV 23:34 reads "they cast lots" in the plural, rendering κλήρους rather than singular κλῆρον.
ASV 23:35 reads "And the rulers also scoffed at him" with no "with them"; the added σὺν αὐτοῖς is unrepresented.

ASV "the Christ of God, his chosen" attaches τοῦ θεοῦ to χριστός and sets ὁ ἐκλεκτός apart, excluding r02 (ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκλεκτός, "the chosen of God"); r00 and r01 differ only in punctuation and remain equally possible.
ἐνέπαιξαν (aorist) and ἐνέπαιζον (imperfect) both give ASV "mocked him"; the English past carries no aspect.
ASV 23:36 reads "coming to him, offering him vinegar" with the participles unjoined; the reading with καί before ὄξος would give "and offering him vinegar".
ASV 23:38 reads "there was also a superscription over him" with no participle "written"; both ἐπιγεγραμμένη and γεγραμμένη would surface as "written over him".
ASV 23:38 has no "in letters of Greek and Latin and Hebrew"; the long addition is unrepresented in the verse.
ASV 23:38 reads "This is the King of the Jews"; the demonstrative renders οὗτός, which the omitting reading lacks at this point.
ASV 23:39 reads "railed on him, saying, Art not thou the Christ?"; "saying" renders λέγων, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV 23:39 puts the taunt as a question, "Art not thou the Christ?", rendering Οὐχί; the Εἰ reading would give a conditional, "If thou art the Christ".
ASV 23:40 reads "and rebuking him said", a participle plus finite verb of speaking, matching ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη; ἐπετίμα αὐτῷ λέγων would give "rebuked him, saying".
ASV 23:42 reads "And he said, Jesus, remember me", addressing Jesus in the vocative; the added dative τῷ Ἰησοῦ would give "said unto Jesus".
ASV 23:42 has no vocative "Lord"; the added κύριε is unrepresented.

ASV 23:42 reads "when thou comest in thy kingdom" and its textual_variant note assigns "into thy kingdom" to some ancient authorities, mapping εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν to the margin and ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ to the text.
ASV 23:43 reads "And he said unto him" with no named subject; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give "And Jesus said unto him".
Pure word order: σοι λέγω and λέγω σοι both give ASV "I say unto thee".
Καὶ ἦν and Ἠν δέ both yield ASV "And it was now about the sixth hour"; the verse note is an alternative_rendering on "land" and decides nothing.
ASV 23:44 reads "it was now about the sixth hour"; "now" renders ἤδη, absent from the omitting reading.

ASV 23:45 reads "the sun’s light failing" with a greek_gloss note "Greek the sun failing" — a genitive absolute, τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος; the finite καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ὁ ἥλιος would give "and the sun was darkened".
ASV "and the veil of the temple was rent" reflects a connective present in either reading (ἐσχίσθη δέ or καὶ ἐσχίσθη); "and" does not choose between them.
ASV 23:46 reads "I commend my spirit" in the present, rendering παρατίθεμαι; the future παραθήσομαι would give "I will commend".
ASV 23:46 reads "and having said this" in the singular, rendering τοῦτο; the plural ταῦτα would give "these things".
ἐδόξαζεν (imperfect) and ἐδόξασεν (aorist) both give ASV "he glorified God".
θεωρήσαντες and θεωροῦντες both come out as ASV "when they beheld the things that were done".
ASV "smiting their breasts" uses the English possessive that a body-part object idiomatically requires; it does not show whether ἑαυτῶν stood with τὰ στήθη.
Dative αὐτῷ (known to him) and genitive αὐτοῦ (his) are both rendered ASV "all his acquaintance".
μακρόθεν and ἀπὸ μακρόθεν are the same adverbial idiom; both give ASV "afar off".
Present συνακολουθοῦσαι and aorist συνακολουθήσασαι both give ASV "that followed with him from Galilee".
ASV 23:50 reads "who was a councillor, a good and righteous man", with the second ἀνήρ unjoined; the reading with καί would give "and a good and righteous man".
ASV 23:51 reads "who was looking for the kingdom of God" with no "he also himself"; the added καὶ ... καὶ αὐτὸς is unrepresented.
ASV 23:53 prints "took it down, and wrapped it"; since one of the two "it"s must be supplied under either reading, the pronoun after "took" does not show whether αὐτὸ stood with καθελὼν.
ASV 23:53 reads "laid him in a tomb" — masculine "him", rendering αὐτόν, where neuter αὐτὸ (agreeing with σῶμα) would give "laid it".
οὐδεὶς οὔπω and οὐδέπω οὐδεὶς are order and spelling variants of one double negative; both give ASV "where never man had yet lain".

ASV "it was the day of the Preparation" renders a genitive after ἡμέρα, excluding r02's nominative Παρασκευή ("the day was the Preparation"); r00 and r01 differ only in punctuation and remain equally possible.
ASV "And the women, who had come with him out of Galilee" supplies the English article the noun phrase requires; the presence of αἱ is not thereby shown.
Pure word order within the phrase; ASV "had come with him out of Galilee" follows English order for a prepositional string and does not track αὐτῷ's position.
